title: Distillation column with reflux control
goal: A process engineer can trace overhead condensation and reflux plus the drum-level and reboiler-temperature control loops.

rubric.must: T-201 connects visibly to E-201, D-201, P-201, LV-201, and back to the column reflux connection.
The column bottom visibly connects to E-202 and a return line visibly reconnects to T-201.
LT-201, LIC-201, and LV-201 form a readable loop at the reflux drum.
TT-202, TIC-202, and TV-202 form a readable electric-and-pneumatic steam control loop.
LV-201 and TV-202 control-valve symbols visibly show diaphragm actuation and FC fail position.
PSV-201 is visibly connected to the column overhead.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the pid exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: All required process paths and control loops are visibly traceable. Overhead vapor flows from T-201 through E-201 and D-201, then through P-201 and FC diaphragm valve LV-201 back to the column. The reboiler circulation, level-control loop, temperature-control loop, and overhead relief connection are all shown.

items.evidence: Visible process lines connect T-201 top to E-201, E-201 to D-201, D-201 bottom to P-201, P-201 through LV-201, and LV-201 back to the column reflux connection.
A DN150 bottoms line visibly connects T-201 bottom to E-202, and a separate DN150 boilup line returns from E-202 to T-201.
LT-201 is shown at D-201, with an electric signal to LIC-201 and a pneumatic command from LIC-201 to LV-201.
TT-202 is shown measuring E-202, with a dashed electric signal to TIC-202 and a pneumatic signal from TIC-202 to the steam valve TV-202.
Both LV-201 and TV-202 visibly use diaphragm-actuated control-valve symbols and are labeled FC.
PSV-201 is visibly branched from the T-201 overhead line and discharges to the line labeled TO ATM.
